question: After the image cache is dropped, how can the module force the on-screen images to re-decode now instead of waiting for the user to navigate?
callsite_evidence: drop_all_cb (0x0c3a7918) frees every cache entry whose reference count (entry+20) is 0 and only skips the ones that are still referenced. An on-screen lv_image widget opens/closes its decoder per draw, so between refresh cycles its cache entry sits at ref 0; the activate-time lv_image_cache_drop(0) therefore already evicts on-screen images. What was missing was forcing the repaint.

_lv_inv_area (0x0c382428) appends an lv_area_t to the display's invalidated-area list (disp+60.., count at disp+604); _lv_display_refr_timer (0x0c38956c) drains that list and repaints on its next tick, re-opening each image file through the installed redirect.

The firmware's own MiWearScreen wake handler async_apply_screen_state_change (0x0c6d096c) uses _lv_inv_area for its 'invalidate screen.' path, confirming it as the supported screen-invalidation primitive.
lv_area_intersect (0x0c3a39b4) clips the requested area to {0,0,hres-1,vres-1}, so passing an oversized area marks exactly the whole active screen dirty without needing the resolution.
control_flow_evidence: The default display is *0x200bd200 and its active screen is disp+24 (lv_display_get_screen_active 0x0c3807bc returns *(disp+24)).
lv_display_is_invalidation_enabled (0x0c380b2c) returns disp+608 > 0; _lv_inv_area no-ops safely when it is 0 (e.g. during a screen-load animation).
_lv_inv_area asserts !disp->rendering_in_progress (bit 1 of disp+58); the module pre-checks that bit and skips the call during a render to avoid the assert path.

In direct/full render mode (disp+57 == 2) _lv_inv_area writes the whole screen as the single invalidated area; in partial mode it appends the clipped area to the list. Both mark the screen for a full repaint.
ownership_analysis: Invalidation only schedules a repaint; it does not rebuild pages or release references. It complements lv_image_cache_drop: the drop evicts the (unreferenced) decoded images, the invalidation makes the refresh timer re-open them through the redirect immediately. A resource still referenced by a live widget (an animation frame, or any font wrapper) is unaffected and still needs the page-rebuild lifecycle. Must run on the UI owner thread and never under the interrupt lock.
unsafe_assumptions: No hardware execution has been performed; the .139 serial console returned no bytes on this host.

Whether a given on-screen image's cache entry is at ref 0 at activate time depends on it not being mid-draw or held open by an animation; genuinely referenced entries survive the drop and are not reloaded by the invalidation.

Display field offsets (act_scr at +24, flags at +58, invalidation-enabled at +608, render mode at +57) are taken from the exact .139 lv_refr.c/lv_display.c decompilation and are not independently field-offset audited on hardware.
recommended_probe: On hardware, confirm that after activate() the whole screen repaints within one refresh tick and that redirected on-screen images (whose entries were unreferenced) show the new resource without a navigation, while animated/referenced images still require navigation.
